cases.attempt: Tried to write a program whose outcome depends on the row. The strongest reading is that 'new features not impacting existing programs' requires a 1985 compiler to keep a 1974-conforming program's meaning for each listed feature. A 1974 program using a listed feature (for example lowercase letters, item 1) shows nothing that this sentence decides: the item's own body clause decides it. A compiler that broke a 1974 program would violate that item's body rule, never this sentence, and 1985 requires no 1974 mode.
cases.reason: The row is one sentence (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 28280). Its main clause, 'The following is a list of the changes of substance included in third Standard COBOL', describes the appendix list. The qualifier 'that are new features not impacting existing programs' classifies the items. The example clause 'for example, a new verb or an additional capability for an old verb' illustrates the classification. No part of it is something a program or a compiler could violate. Every change it introduces is required by its own body clause, and the listed items are rows of their own (for example 1985-GR-B.2.1-48). The quotation lies in the row's own text (the reader's cite_check OK), and the 'describes the standard's ...' form fits a row about the document.
